# Current owner-approved research goal

Updated 2026-09-04 during the GPT-6 successor handoff. This objective governs the current research work alongside ADR-0018 and the frozen experiment protocols. The native successor goal was created before this wording arrived; its API supports status changes only, so its shorter objective remains active rather than being falsely completed or blocked to replace it.

Build and independently validate a useful NFL prediction engine for the owner's hobby and educational analytics site, following the approved research-first master-plan revision. Prioritize (1) football-only joint team-score forecasts with naive, SRS and Elo comparisons; (2) player participation, opportunity and performance projections once data admission supports a valid population; and (3) properly timestamped market-value comparisons after the football model is frozen and provider access is separately authorized. Assess build-versus-buy honestly against named, reproducible, timestamp-compatible benchmarks; treat the owner's 1%+ improvement ambition as a hypothesis to test, never as promised performance.

Current first milestone: preregister RF-02S as a numerical-only successor, qualify the mean-matching solver on prior successes and preserved failures, then run the unchanged chronological team-score/Elo backtest to an independently reviewed scorecard and decision. Preserve RF-02's terminal protocol_invalid result and RF-04's blocked player-data admission; do not lower thresholds to force acceptance.

Use rolling-origin evaluation, training-fold-only transforms, paired uncertainty, calibration/coverage, ablations, leakage checks and falsification before promotion. Keep periodic quality and usefulness checkpoints that reassess the experiment, agent assignments, compute cost and the next decision. Use graphs only where they improve dependency/provenance checks or survive preregistered predictive testing. Learning loops may automatically refresh state, but changes to model structure or hyperparameters require frozen experiments and out-of-sample evidence.

Proceed autonomously through safe, authorized research steps and keep the master plan current. Do not access provider secrets, credential files, environment inventories, Odds API/quota paths, or change the interface, deployments or production forecasts under the present scope. Park infrastructure work until needed for a concrete integration or release gate. Continue until the authorized research yields a reviewable, evidence-backed result and explicit next decisions; retain broader product work as outstanding wherever separate data, integration or release requirements remain.

## Completion boundary clarification

Preserve the full intended product outcome: continue toward an independently tested NFL prediction tool ready for the owner to view the page and give feedback, or stop only at an unavoidable external action or authorization boundary. A completed scorecard is a milestone, not completion of the overall goal. Current no-interface, no-deployment and no-provider restrictions remain in force until their applicable authority exists.

# Prediction Engine Operating System

## Active authority — research-first revision

The [current owner-approved research goal](RESEARCH-GOAL.md), updated at the GPT-6 handoff on 2026-09-04, governs the successor work. It explicitly includes honest build-versus-buy evaluation and treats 1%+ improvement as an unproven hypothesis.

RF-02S numerical qualification and wrapper now have independent acceptance. The one unchanged chronological replay stopped at its32-game pilot cost gate (9427.09seconds projected versus7200 permitted); terminal audits passed and the full scorecard remains unavailable. No restart or budget increase. The overall endpoint remains a tested tool ready for page feedback or an unavoidable external/authorization boundary; a scorecard alone does not complete it.

On 2026-09-03 the owner approved [ADR-0018](ADR-0018-research-first.md): **team-score research → player projections → market-value comparisons**, with rigorous statistical tests and a smaller local research workflow. `config/research-first.v1.json` is the versioned scope record. This is the active execution order; the original production architecture below is retained as the release design, not a prerequisite for offline model research.

Current work: **the independently preregistered RF-02C exact scoring-cache successor**, after RF-04's actual data gate blocked the historical player fit. RF-02 remains terminal `protocol_invalid`; RF-02S qualified that numerical repair but then hit its frozen pilot cost gate. RF-02C may only cache repeated CDF calculations while retaining every football, fold, metric, promotion and resource rule. The team-score comparison is still unresolved because RF-02 stopped before any outer evaluation game. Full D1/R2 migration, recovery, packaging and release qualification remain parked. No provider access, production change or model promotion is authorized.

**RF-04 blocked data gate:** The owner-approved capture now verifies 47 objects, 415,424,308 bytes and 1,822,954 rows with zero-request replay. The corrected leakage-safe lagged-roster cohort covers only 83.78% of realized WR targets and leaves 21.66% of its player-games unresolved; no season clears both 95% coverage thresholds. Historical Tuesday population timing and independent zero/DNP truth remain unproven. [Actual result](research-first/RF-04-DATA-ADMISSION.v2.md). No player model or complete population is accepted.

**RF-02 terminal checkpoint:** The frozen implementation at `4a28330` passed 83 synthetic tests and then actually fit historical data. At 2011 Week 8 its baseline distribution solver hit floating-point stagnation above the frozen tolerance. Two independent reviewers confirmed the failure and exact output integrity. Zero of 3,407 outer games were evaluated. No model was accepted or rejected on accuracy; no automatic restart is permitted. The earlier [implementation receipt](research-first/RF-02-IMPLEMENTATION.v2.md) is preserved as pre-run history.

**Historical pre-fit checkpoint:** Before this run, the complete v2 protocol and new-data admission passed distinct quantitative and temporal reviews and 48 focused tests. All 3,407 scored targets were retained; only as-of-unavailable prior inputs were deferred. The 12h retrospective assumption and 24h sensitivity are explicit, not verified original publication. [RF-01's acceptance](research-first/RF-01-ACCEPTANCE.v2.json) remains bounded to pre-fit admission. Old drafts/missing-source receipts and rejected experiments remain preserved.

**Graph and benchmark direction:** use existing-manifest ancestry checks, SRS graph-equivalence tests, and later independently tested player-role relationships. No graph database/GNN is a prerequisite. A minimum 1% improvement claim requires a named common-game benchmark, uncertainty supporting that minimum, calibration and prospective confirmation; plumbing tests do not demonstrate predictive gain. See [graph and learning-loop research](research-first/GRAPH-AND-BENCHMARK-RESEARCH.md).

## Core value

Create an artifact-driven prediction operating system that can prove what was knowable at each forecast origin, let small statistical modules earn their place, publish one coherent game-outcome distribution, and measure whether the output improves human judgment.

The system is not one expanding model. It is a controlled graph of data, experiments, model packages, forecasts, evaluations, and promotion decisions.

Execution is governed by `QUALITY-GATES.md`. Every package must show that it closes an acceptance requirement, changes a decision through falsification, or removes a concrete blocker on the path to team-score, player, or market-value evidence. Deep independent alignment checks run at phase boundaries, after three package attempts, after a repeated failure, or after another 500,000 observable goal tokens. Work that mainly validates its own process is simplified or stopped.

## Fixed truths

- Model Laboratory Module 1 ended `reject_all`. C0 is a research benchmark only.
- Model Laboratory Module 2 ended `reject_all`. P0 is a research benchmark only.
- Module 2B remains parked and unauthorized until its own R1-v2 target audit passes. The new RF direct-score lane does not depend on it and cannot reuse it as accepted evidence.
- All historical results through 2025 are research-exposed. They cannot be called pristine confirmation data again.
- The 2026 pre-kickoff forecast archive is the next honest confirmation stream.
- If the 2026 archive activates after Week 1, it is partial-season shadow evidence from its actual activation time; missing earlier weeks are never backfilled as prospective forecasts.
- The football-only model cannot use market prices, line movement, public betting, or recorded selections as features.
- Market comparison begins only after a football-only forecast is frozen.
- The system is self-updating under frozen rules. It is not allowed to select features or tune structure from in-season outcomes.
- Human adjustments and selected-opportunity outcomes never enter model training.

## Existing assets to preserve

- Cloudflare Worker and D1 operational runtime
- nflverse, odds, injuries, weather, pregame-context, and sentiment adapters
- staging, idempotency, quota, freshness, alert, and last-good behavior
- point-in-time, provenance, experiment, model-registry, forecast, and evaluation contracts
- Module 1 and Module 2 offline laboratories and their frozen negative results
- joint-score, market translation, power de-vig, scenario, probabilistic evaluation, and model-gate libraries
- governance configs, 52 research questions, ADRs, and the Novelty Charter

## Accepted operational foundations

- OS-15A qualifies the dormant, provider-free interim scheduler for the five accepted OS-02A horizons. Deterministic trigger and job identities, fenced renewable leases, duplicate convergence, strict pre-deadline persistence, contemporaneous withholding, heartbeat/watchdog recovery, reschedule handling, and a versioned OS-15 cutover contract passed local and isolated hosted qualification.
- A separate authenticated direct-D1 acceptance audit verified the preserved OS-01A/OS-19A schema objects, append-only guards, exact 38/462 bootstrap, zero outstanding reservations, and empty OS-02A/OS-15A production tables. It overruled a stale bounded database-viewer projection without changing the database.
- The bounded provider-independent OS-03A storage mechanism is accepted. Exact response bytes, canonical secret-redacted request identities, content-addressed D1/R2 manifests and sidecars, append-only events, failure alerts, last-good preservation, corruption quarantine, deterministic retry, and provider-offline replay passed twice on an isolated owner-only Sites D1/R2 resource with zero provider calls, secret reads, or quota reservations.
- The clean OS-13A successor qualifies the dormant append-only forecast-or-withheld ledger mechanism. Its hardened D1/R2 path passed exact-byte publication and recovery, deterministic duplicate convergence, overlapping-worker publication, lease-expiry reclamation and stale-worker fencing, corruption refusal and restoration, and empty-only rollback across all five horizon identities on a clean owner-only hosted resource. The rejected first attempt remains immutable non-evidence.
- OS-01 Generations 10 through 14 retain their bounded hosted catalog, foreign-key, row-count, content-root, and physical-prestate evidence. The single quality-gated normal-path successor then proved that the exact parser-compatible `0000`–`0020` projection reaches the expected fresh blank Sites D1 state: 93 application tables, 127 autoindexes, 76 triggers, 54 foreign-key rows with zero violations, eight semantic receipts, 20 platform receipts, `quick_check=ok`, and zero application data rows. Exact response bytes and an independent audit are preserved under `.planning/engine-os/execution/os-01/normal-path-parser-compat-successor/`. This closes only projected-chain blank compatibility and ends migration microgenerations. Parser-compatible authority versioning, populated-forward preservation, platform recovery, runtime-DDL exclusion, production parity, ARC-03, full OS-01, migration, and production authority remain unaccepted.
- These bounded results start no prospective stream and accept neither a live connector nor the complete forecast-ledger requirement. Full OS-03A, OS-03, OS-04, OS-13B, OS-15, and the remaining OS-18A credential/provider gates remain required before authenticated acquisition or production activation.

## Preserved platform stop; research direction now approved

The single cohesive v3 local packet remains `rejected_no_production_action`; its exact empty rollback identity gate failed despite preserved rows, receipts, foreign keys, and integrity. The independent quality gate still stops OS-01 implementation. Preserve all prior bounded evidence and the rejection under `execution/os-01/v3-local-closure/`; no new migration generation or historical SQL/verifier change. The owner's explicit approval is now recorded in ADR-0018: resume a separate local research lane, not this platform packet. No predictive requirement is closed by the amendment.

## Gaps identified when the plan was created

The accepted-foundations and current-state records govern which of these original gaps are already boundedly addressed; this list is not a current acceptance claim.

1. The active Worker and D1 control plane coexists with a second Supabase job path.
2. Migrations and runtime `CREATE TABLE` statements both claim schema authority.
3. Production manifests often preserve hashes but not durable raw source bytes.
4. The Python laboratory cannot yet export a package the TypeScript registry can verify and run.
5. The market-free forecast ledger is coupled to market freshness through decision-board construction.
6. The public board can initiate background maintenance.
7. No canonical as-of identity service joins player, roster, snap, injury, venue, and provider IDs.
8. Heavy refits and bootstrap work are assigned to a Worker runtime without a separate compute contract.
9. Monitoring still mixes all-game forecast evaluation with legacy selected-play reporting.
10. There is no validated market-free production candidate.
11. Ephemeral 2026 raw, issued-weather, exact-quote, and forecast-or-withheld evidence must be captured before the full platform refactor finishes.

## Retained production architecture — not the local research prerequisite

```text
External sources
      |
Source connectors and validation
      |
Content-addressed raw objects in R2
      |
D1 source manifest, identities, and publication state
      |
Point-in-time replay and feature factory
      |
Research laboratory and frozen experiment registry
      |
Verified model package and model registry
      |
Scheduled market-free forecast compiler
      |

Forecast ledger ------- Market snapshot ledger
      |                         |
Outcome evaluation ---- Model-market comparison
      \                         /
        Versioned publication snapshot
                    |
             Read-only public API
```

## State ownership

- RF research uses named immutable local football objects, a locked Python runtime, frozen protocols and append-only result bundles. Local reproducibility is not prospective timing or production durability. See ADR-0018 for the research/activation/release boundary.
- Git stores code, configuration, feature definitions, protocols, and small manifests.
- R2 stores raw source bytes, versioned Parquet data, large forecast grids, and model packages.
- D1 stores identities, manifests, job state, compact online features, registry metadata, forecast summaries, evaluations, and serving pointers.
- Python plus a locked analytical runtime runs historical laboratories and heavy fitting.
- Cloudflare Worker runs lightweight ingestion coordination, inference, publication, and read serving.
- A separate authenticated compute runner performs full-history refits, large bootstraps, and artifact publication.

## Non-goals

- No interface redesign in this roadmap.
- No automatic wagering or user-specific pick system.
- No autonomous feature search or in-season structural tuning.
- No second production database, hosted feature store, Kafka, or warehouse without measured need.
- No paid data dependency without an explicit coverage, rights, and cost decision.
- No public-versus-sharp claim without timestamp and source-population validation.
- No single unexplained confidence number.

## Definition of done

Research progress means an audited target, a frozen question, a common-game scorecard and a decision that improves the next experiment. A rejected challenger with a retained labeled benchmark is a valid research outcome; it is not a production forecast or betting-value claim. Player projections and market comparison have separate scorecards and cannot rescue a rejected football model.

The operating system is ready when every scheduled game has either a pre-kickoff market-free forecast or an explicit withholding record, every input and model package is replayable from immutable artifacts, all-game outcomes are scored prospectively, market comparison is attached without modifying the football forecast, promotion follows frozen gates, failures preserve last good output, and the site reads one precomputed publication snapshot without causing writes or provider spend.

- [ ] **FB-01 — Drive-state ontology.** Regulation drives and terminal states are reconstructed and reconciled independently, with overtime stored separately.

- [ ] **FB-08 — Clock, regulation, and overtime.** Possession timing, end-of-half behavior, kneels, game-state rules, ties, and era-specific overtime are explicit simulation mechanics.

- [ ] **SCORE-01 — Earned composition.** The compiler may use only modules that passed their own gate or were explicitly declared nuisance components before the comparison.
- [ ] **SCORE-02 — Normalized joint distribution.** The engine emits a valid joint home-away score distribution, not just two point estimates.
- [ ] **SCORE-03 — Coherent derived outcomes.** Win, tie, margin, total, means, quantiles, covariance, and cover/push/total probabilities on fixed model-independent grids reconcile to the same joint distribution; actual posted contracts and prices enter only in the market layer.
- [ ] **SCORE-04 — Integration falsification.** Component removal, double-counting checks, residual diagnostics, era checks, and scenario sensitivity seek to invalidate the assembled engine.
- [ ] **SCORE-05 — Frozen football decision.** The engine earns `reject_all` or prospective `shadow_eligible` under a preregistered scorecard; complexity is rejected when its gain is unstable.

- [ ] **CONF-01 — Reliability vector.** Confidence is represented by predictive coverage, ensemble disagreement, data quality, distribution shift, and scenario sensitivity, not by model-market disagreement or one opaque score.
- [ ] **CONF-02 — Scenario robustness.** Forecasts identify robust, fragile, and indeterminate conclusions across plausible pregame scenarios without pretending scenario probabilities are known when they are not.

- [ ] **CONF-04 — Human judgment is auditable and separate.** Manual interpretation and overrides are immutable annotations that can be reviewed but never become football-model training labels.
- [ ] **CONF-05 — Controlled learning loop.** Weekly state changes follow frozen rules; drift can alert or withhold, coefficient changes require a logged gate, and structure changes only in offseason review.
